sentences.en: This is the record-breaking, Kickstarter-funded Season 3 of 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听创下纪录、通过众筹资金制作的《99%隐形》第三季。

sentences.en: Give yourself a round of applause.
sentences.zh: 为自己鼓个掌吧。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Pneumatic.
sentences.zh: 气动。

sentences.en: Pneumatic.
sentences.zh: 气动。

sentences.en: Pneumatic tubes, of or pertaining to air, gases, or wind.
sentences.zh: 气动管道，与空气、气体或风有关或属于它们。

sentences.en: Oh, good, you're here.
sentences.zh: 哦，太好了，你在这儿。

sentences.en: Donnie, we found some tubes in the wall, and now we're trying to see where the tubes go.
sentences.zh: 唐妮，我们在墙里发现了一些管道，现在我们正试图弄清楚这些管道通往哪里。

sentences.en: You see, things go away, and they never come back.
sentences.zh: 你看，东西运走了，就再也没有回来过。

sentences.en: How the heck does it work?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: I guess we'll never know.
sentences.zh: 我想我们永远也不会知道了。

sentences.en: Vacuum!
sentences.zh: 真空！

sentences.en: Yeah, right, vacuum.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，真空。

sentences.en: Let her rip.
sentences.zh: 开始吧。

sentences.en: In the world before telephone and email, the task of transmitting information and moving material objects was essentially the same challenge.
sentences.zh: 在没有电话和电子邮件的世界里，传输信息和移动实体物品的任务本质上是同一个挑战。

sentences.en: The way you sent someone a message was pretty much the same process as sending someone a package.
sentences.zh: 你给某人发消息的方式，和给某人寄包裹的过程几乎是一样的。

sentences.en: You had to send a piece of physical media through the post, or on a ship.
sentences.zh: 你必须通过邮局或乘船发送一件实体媒介。

sentences.en: It was the telegraph that divided telling someone something from giving someone something.
sentences.zh: 正是电报将“告诉某人某事”与“给某人某物”区分了开来。

sentences.en: But remember, everyday people didn't speak Morse code, so the message had to be deciphered, written on a slip of paper, and then it was delivered to the recipient.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，普通人不会说摩斯密码，所以必须将信息译解，写在纸条上，然后再送达收件人手中。

sentences.en: Pneumatic.
sentences.zh: 气动。

sentences.en: Even though you can probably guess already that electronic communication eventually killed most of the need for pneumatic tubes,
sentences.zh: 尽管你可能已经猜到，电子通信最终消除了对气动管道的大部分需求，

sentences.en: you may not know that it was the telegraph itself that also put pneumatic tubes into widespread use.
sentences.zh: 但你可能不知道，正是电报本身也让气动管道得到了广泛应用。

sentences.en: As telegrams blew up and the cost dropped and the volume rose, it became very difficult to quickly deliver them to their destinations.
sentences.zh: 随着电报业务的爆发、成本的下降以及数量的增加，如何将它们快速送到目的地变得非常困难。

sentences.en: And so what they needed to do was come up with another way to get messages across the city quickly.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们需要做的是想出另一种方法，让信息快速穿梭于城市之间。

sentences.en: So if you can't send something with that newfangled electricity stuff, you have to figure out a way to do it old school, sending a message as a physical object.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你不能用那种时髦的电力玩意儿发送东西，你就得想办法用老式的方法，把信息当作实体对象来发送。

sentences.en: It's a last mile problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个最后一公里问题。

sentences.en: Getting to an end customer or an end recipient can be the more difficult problem.
sentences.zh: 触达最终客户或最终收件人可能才是更困难的问题。

sentences.en: And they came up with the post pneumatic or the pneumatic post as a means of doing that.
sentences.zh: 于是他们想出了气动邮政或气动邮件来作为实现这一目标的手段。

sentences.en: That is Molly Wright Steenson, researcher, PhD student, and aficionada of all things pneumatic tube.
sentences.zh: 那是莫莉·赖特·斯廷森，研究员、博士生，也是气动管道的狂热爱好者。

sentences.en: Pneumatic tubes are systems of subterranean urban postal services that delivered messages underneath cities all across the world in major financial centers.
sentences.zh: 气动管道是地下城市邮政服务系统，在世界各大金融中心的城市地下投递信件。

sentences.en: Those were the large-scale implementations.
sentences.zh: 那些是大规模的应用。

sentences.en: But later on, there are a number of smaller pneumatic tube systems more familiar to people today.
sentences.zh: 但后来，出现了一些较小的气动管道系统，人们今天更为熟悉。

sentences.en: Our producer Sam Greenspan spoke with Molly through a different series of tubes.
sentences.zh: 我们的制作人萨姆·格林斯潘通过另一套管道与莫莉进行了交谈。

sentences.en: So it turns out Molly and I had similar experiences with pneumatic tubes growing up.
sentences.zh: 原来莫莉和我有着相似的成长经历，都接触过气动管道。

sentences.en: When I was a kid, we used to go to the bank down the street and...
sentences.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，我们经常去街角的银行，然后……

sentences.en: I remember going to the bank with my dad.
sentences.zh: 我记得我和爸爸一起去银行。

sentences.en: We'd go to the drive-thru and he'd put his deposit slip or whatever inside this plastic canister.
sentences.zh: 我们会去免下车窗口，他会把存款单什么的放进这个塑料罐里。

sentences.en: My mom would unroll her window and she'd get the canister from this big air-making device.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈会摇下车窗，从这个巨大的造气装置里拿到罐子。

sentences.en: And she'd put in whatever checks she wanted to deposit.
sentences.zh: 然后她把她想存的支票放进去。

sentences.en: And then I would see it shoot up.
sentences.zh: 接着我就会看到它冲上去。

sentences.en: Sucked up through this clear tube.
sentences.zh: 被吸进这个透明的管道里。

sentences.en: Through this clear tube.
sentences.zh: 穿过这个透明的管道。

sentences.en: And it would shoot across to the bank.
sentences.zh: 然后它会飞射到银行。

sentences.en: And then the ladies in the bank...
sentences.zh: 接着银行里的女士们……

sentences.en: To tell her tonight, put in some candy or a matchbox car.
sentences.zh: 今晚告诉她，放进一些糖果或火柴盒小汽车。

sentences.en: Lollipops for me and my brothers.
sentences.zh: 给我和兄弟们的棒棒糖。

sentences.en: And dog biscuits for the dog.
sentences.zh: 还有给狗狗的狗饼干。

sentences.en: And send it over with my dad's receipt.
sentences.zh: 连同我爸爸的收据一起送过来。

sentences.en: Back by a pneumatic tube.
sentences.zh: 通过气动管道送回。

sentences.en: And it just seemed...
sentences.zh: 而它看起来……

sentences.en: Just seemed really cool.
sentences.zh: 看起来真的很酷。

sentences.en: It seemed kind of magic.
sentences.zh: 感觉有点像魔法。

sentences.en: And they also hearken back to another era.
sentences.zh: 它们也让人回想起另一个时代。

sentences.en: You may only know about pneumatic tubes in the context of a bank drive-thru.
sentences.zh: 你可能只在银行的免下车窗口这种背景下了解气动管道。

sentences.en: But when they were invented, they really set the stage for what communication would look like over the next century.
sentences.zh: 但当它们被发明出来时，确实为接下来一个世纪的通信面貌奠定了基础。

sentences.en: The pneumatic post first started in London in 1853.
sentences.zh: 气动邮政最早于1853年在伦敦起步。

sentences.en: But the technology transferred very quickly to other cities.
sentences.zh: 但这项技术很快传到了其他城市。

sentences.en: Vienna, Marseille, Munich, Milan, Berlin, Philadelphia, New York, St. Louis, Buenos Aires, Australia.
sentences.zh: 维也纳、马赛、慕尼黑、米兰、柏林、费城、纽约、圣路易斯、布宜诺斯艾利斯、澳大利亚。

sentences.en: In fact, there were pneumatic post systems in every major financial city on every continent with the exception of Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 事实上，除了南极洲，各大洲的每个主要金融城市都有气动邮政系统。

sentences.en: Antarctica's always slacken.
sentences.zh: 南极洲总是这么懒散。

sentences.en: But nowhere were pneumatic tubes more extensive than in Paris.
sentences.zh: 但气动管道规模最大、最完善的地方莫过于巴黎。

sentences.en: At the end of the 19th century, Baron Haussmann had totally redone Paris' urban layout, putting in those big iconic boulevards and circular plazas.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪末，奥斯曼男爵彻底重塑了巴黎的城市布局，修建了那些标志性的大道和环形广场。

sentences.en: And he also put in sewers.
sentences.zh: 他还铺设了下水道。

sentences.en: So not only did the sewer carry potable water and eventually electrical cables, but it carried pneumatic tubes.
sentences.zh: 因此，下水道不仅输送饮用水和后来的电缆，还铺设了气动管道。

sentences.en: And these tubes inside of tubes were a hit.
sentences.zh: 这种管道套管道的设计大获成功。

sentences.en: By 1919, Paris was processing 12 million pieces of pneumatic post a year.
sentences.zh: 到1919年，巴黎每年处理1200万件气动邮件。

sentences.en: And by 1945, there were 450 kilometers of pneumatic tubing lining Paris' underground,
sentences.zh: 到1945年，巴黎地下排列着450公里的气动管道，

sentences.en: making it possible to get a handwritten note across Paris in less than two hours without even breaking a sweat.
sentences.zh: 让人甚至毫不费力就能在不到两个小时的时间里将手写便条送达巴黎各地。

sentences.en: Here's how it worked.
sentences.zh: 运作方式是这样的。

sentences.en: You write something on some special stationery and close it in a special envelope, pay special postage,
sentences.zh: 你在某种特殊的信纸上写下内容，装进特殊的信封，支付特殊的邮资，

sentences.en: and you get it to your local 2BeaSt.
sentences.zh: 然后把它交给你当地的2BeaSt。

sentences.en: That's what you call one of the people who sends pneumatic poSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是对发送气动邮件的人的称呼。

sentences.en: 2Beast puts the envelope in a canister.
sentences.zh: 2Beast把信封放进罐子里。

sentences.en: And let me tell you about these canisters.
sentences.zh: 让我来跟你讲讲这些罐子。

sentences.en: At first, they just looked like soup cans.
sentences.zh: 起初，它们看起来就像汤罐头。

sentences.en: But over time, they became more aerodynamic and began to resemble little rockets.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，它们变得更加符合空气动力学，开始像一枚枚小火箭。

sentences.en: Anyway, the 2Beast rings an electric bell to alert the 2Beast on the receiving end that there's an incoming canister,
sentences.zh: 总之，2Beast会按响电铃，提醒收件端的2Beast有进站的罐子，

sentences.en: and then, thump, it's hurtling through Paris' underbelly so fast that the sending 2Beast could actually hear the canister arriving at its destination.
sentences.zh: 然后，伴随着砰的一声，它以极快的速度在巴黎的腹地穿梭，以至于发送端的2Beast甚至能听到罐子到达目的地的声音。

sentences.en: The descriptions that I've read from the 19th century talk about the shock,
sentences.zh: 我读过的19世纪的描述中谈到了这种冲击力，

sentences.en: the noise of the shock of the pneumatic post arriving.
sentences.zh: 气动邮件到达时的冲击噪音。

sentences.en: The only mechanism that could provide enough force would be steam.
sentences.zh: 唯一能提供足够动力的机制是蒸汽。

sentences.en: And so there were gigantic steam engines underneath the Hotel des Postes,
sentences.zh: 因此，巴黎中央邮局圣邮政局下方有巨大的蒸汽机，

sentences.en: which was the central post office in Paris,
sentences.zh: 这就是巴黎的中心邮局，

sentences.en: and they would produce the compressed and rarefied air that would serve to push or pull the pneumatic tubes
sentences.zh: 它们产生压缩空气和稀薄空气，用来推动或拉动气动管道，

sentences.en: through all of the kilometers and miles and miles of tubes that were underneath the streets.
sentences.zh: 穿过街道下方数不清英里长的管道。

sentences.en: There were also even buildings that just simply existed to produce air for the tube services.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一些建筑物存在的唯一目的就是为管道服务制造空气。

sentences.en: The biggest pneumatic tube systems had problems that required some creative troubleshooting.
sentences.zh: 最大的气动管道系统也遇到了需要进行创造性排障的问题。

sentences.en: Paris had an interesting mechanism in case there was a blockage.
sentences.zh: 巴黎有一种有趣的机制来应对堵塞。

sentences.en: Someone would fire a gun into the tube and then measure the sound waves
sentences.zh: 有人会向管道里开枪，然后测量声波，

sentences.en: and be able to figure out to within, I guess, 2 meters or so where the blockage was.
sentences.zh: 就能弄清楚堵塞物在哪个位置，误差大概在2米以内。

sentences.en: And then they would be able to go underground and undo the flange and bring out the offending canister.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就能下到地下，拆开法兰，取出惹事的罐子。

sentences.en: I guess it's better than what happened in Berlin where they just poured copious amounts of wine
sentences.zh: 我想这比柏林的情况要好，在柏林，人们只是将大量的葡萄酒倾倒进管道里，

sentences.en: into the tubes in order to unfreeze the stuck canisters.
sentences.zh: 以此来解冻卡住的罐子。

sentences.en: As exciting as all this sounds, electric communication evolved.
sentences.zh: 尽管这一切听起来令人兴奋，但电子通信还是发展了起来。

sentences.en: In Europe, other technologies like telephone and Telefax improved and got way cheaper.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲，电话和传真等其他技术不断改进，变得便宜得多。

sentences.en: And solved the last mile problem.
sentences.zh: 并且解决了最后一公里问题。

sentences.en: But it was another form of physical transport that put the nail in the coffin.
sentences.zh: 但却是另一种形式的实体运输给它们敲响了丧钟。

sentences.en: The thing that put them out of business in the United States was the invention of the truck.
sentences.zh: 在美国让它们倒闭的是卡车的发明。

sentences.en: The truck was invented in 1912 and that's kind of what did it.
sentences.zh: 卡车于1912年被发明出来，基本上就是它干的。

sentences.en: Trucks are fine and all, but they just don't capture the imagination like a massive pneumatic tube network.
sentences.zh: 卡车虽然挺好，但它们就是无法像庞大的气动管道网络那样激发想象力。

sentences.en: As silly as such a thing might seem today.
sentences.zh: 尽管今天看来这种东西可能很傻。

sentences.en: Molly and I spent a good deal of time trying to figure out what exactly it is about the tubes
sentences.zh: 莫莉和我花了大量时间试图弄清楚，管道究竟有什么魔力，

sentences.en: that leads us to be fascinated with them.
sentences.zh: 让我们对它们如此着迷。

sentences.en: I have a couple of theories about why pneumatic tubes are magic.
sentences.zh: 我有几个关于为什么气动管道是魔法的理论。

sentences.en: I think they inspire wonder because they're alive or it feels like they're alive.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们激发了惊叹，因为它们是有生命的，或者感觉它们是有生命的。

sentences.en: They're reaching out through the city.
sentences.zh: 它们向整个城市伸出触角。

sentences.en: They have tendrils and tentacles and they breathe and they throw things up and they feel much, much bigger than we are.
sentences.zh: 它们长着卷须和触手，它们会呼吸，会把东西抛出来，感觉比我们大得多、宏伟得多。

sentences.en: I also think they inspire wonder because they manifest communication.
sentences.zh: 我还认为它们激发了惊叹，因为它们具象化了沟通。

sentences.en: You know, for us today, when we think of communication, all the ones and zeros and digital things that we move don't feel real tangible to us anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对我们今天来说，当我们想到通信时，我们传输的所有1和0以及数字化的东西对我们来说已经不再真实具体了。

sentences.en: But I also think that they felt pretty magical to people back then, too, that they were kind of electrical and breathing connections of communication.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，对于当时的人们来说，它们也相当神奇，它们是某种通电且会呼吸的通信连接。

sentences.en: You could scent a handkerchief and send it to your lover via pneumatic tube and it would still smell like you.
sentences.zh: 你可以给手帕喷上香水，通过气动管道寄给你的爱人，它依然会有你的气味。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I think they were romantic as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我认为它们也是浪漫的。

sentences.en: And I think that that's part of the wonder today, too.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是当今这种奇妙感受的一部分。

sentences.en: So, in a sense, they're both alive and mechanical, both high and low tech.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种意义上说，它们既有生命又机械，既是高科技也是低科技。

sentences.en: And there's also something to be said about the journey of a tube canister that you can imagine it snaking its way through these underground passageways carrying your message.
sentences.zh: 关于管道罐的旅程也有话要说，你可以想象它在这些地下通道中蜿蜒前行，运送着你的信息。

sentences.en: And so this idea of being able to go somewhere where you wouldn't otherwise be able to go is amazing.
sentences.zh: 所以这种能够去到你原本去不了的地方的想法是惊人的。

sentences.en: That tube message has made that entire underworld journey in order to surface in the hands of its recipient.
sentences.zh: 那个管道信息完成了整个地下世界的旅程，最终浮现在收件人的手中。

sentences.en: More than their widespread use, what might be the most surprising thing about pneumatic tube systems is how long they stayed in use.
sentences.zh: 比起它们的广泛应用，关于气动管道系统最令人惊讶的可能是它们维持使用的时间有多长。

sentences.en: The post-pneumatique operated in Paris until as late as 1964.
sentences.zh: 巴黎的气动邮政系统一直运营到1964年。

sentences.en: Tubes even ran over the Brooklyn Bridge until 1953.
sentences.zh: 管道甚至一直运行到1953年的布鲁克林大桥上。

sentences.en: And it took a force of nature to knock them out of Prague.
sentences.zh: 而且需要一场大自然的力量才能让它们在布拉格退役。

sentences.en: That city was using them until a flood in 2002.
sentences.zh: 那个城市一直在使用它们，直到2002年发生了一场洪水。

sentences.en: But get this, lots of places still use pneumatic tubes.
sentences.zh: 但你得知道，很多地方仍然在使用气动管道。

sentences.en: Hospitals use pneumatic tube systeMs.
sentences.zh: 医院使用气动管道系统。

sentences.en: And that's because you really can't digitize tissue or medication.
sentences.zh: 这是因为你真的无法将人体组织或药物数字化。

sentences.en: And so the next time you find yourself in a hospital, take a look because you'll find them by the nurse's stations and in the emergency room.
sentences.zh: 所以下次当你身处医院时，留意一下，因为你会在护士站旁和急诊室里找到它们。

sentences.en: They're also used at places at grocery stores or big electronics stores.
sentences.zh: 它们也被用在杂货店或大型电子产品商店等地方。

sentences.en: Usually that kind of delivery of all of the money through pneumatic tubes so that it's not anywhere where the store could get robbed.
sentences.zh: 通常是通过气动管道输送所有的现金，这样它们就不会出现在商店可能被抢劫的任何地方。

sentences.en: When Molly was doing research on tubes at the New York City Public Library, she found that her requests were being dispatched via a pneumatic tube.
sentences.zh: 当莫莉在纽约公共图书馆研究管道时，她发现她的索书请求是通过气动管道发送的。

sentences.en: But there's one other tube system in New York that moves a lot more material.
sentences.zh: 但纽约还有另一个管道系统，能够运输更多的物质。

sentences.en: In Roosevelt Island, pneumatic tubes are used for garbage.
sentences.zh: 在罗斯福岛，气动管道被用来处理垃圾。

sentences.en: Roosevelt Island, if you don't know, is a small island in the East River between Manhattan and Queens in New York.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道的话，罗斯福岛是纽约曼哈顿和皇后区之间东河中的一个小岛。

sentences.en: And as it happens, my good friend Hannah Jamal grew up there.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，我的好朋友汉娜·贾马尔在那里长大。

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 嘿。

sentences.en: Hey, Hannah.
sentences.zh: 嘿，汉娜。

sentences.en: How's it going?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Nice to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴听到你的声音。

sentences.en: So I called up Hannah and asked her about the pneumatic tubes in her hometown.
sentences.zh: 所以我打电话给汉娜，向她询问她家乡的气动管道。

sentences.en: I get flustered when people ask me about the garbage tubes because, to me, how you take out your trash on Roosevelt Island is not the most fascinating thing about it.
sentences.zh: 当人们问我关于垃圾管道的事时，我会感到局促，因为对我来说，在罗斯福岛上如何倒垃圾并不是它最迷人的地方。

sentences.en: Yes, I am sure that there are thousands of fascinating facts about Roosevelt Island, but let's hear about those garbage tubes.
sentences.zh: 是的，我相信关于罗斯福岛有成千上万个迷人的事实，但让我们听听那些垃圾管道的事吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Roosevelt Island is only about three miles long and about 800 feet wide.
sentences.zh: 对，罗斯福岛只有大约三英里长，大约800英尺宽。

sentences.en: And when the island was being developed for residential living in the 1960s, planners determined that the quality of life would be better without big garbage trucks on the roads.
sentences.zh: 当这个岛在20世纪60年代被开发用于住宅生活时，规划人员确定，如果没有大型垃圾卡车在路上行驶，生活质量会更好。

sentences.en: I know, right?
sentences.zh: 我知道，对吧？

sentences.en: So instead, they dispatched with their trash with a pneumatic tube network.
sentences.zh: 所以相反，他们用气动管道网络来处理垃圾。

sentences.en: And I have one friend in particular.
sentences.zh: 我有一个特别的朋友。

sentences.en: He's my friend, David.
sentences.zh: 他是我的朋友，大卫。

sentences.en: And he can tell you more about how it works.
sentences.zh: 他可以告诉你更多关于它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: So I asked Brooklyn-based producer Muj Zady to go meet Hannah's friend.
sentences.zh: 所以我请总部位于布鲁克林的制作人穆杰·扎迪去见汉娜的朋友。

sentences.en: Oh, hey.
sentences.zh: 哦，嘿。

sentences.en: How's it going, Muj?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样，穆杰？

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: A guy named David Kimball Stanley.
sentences.zh: 一个叫大卫·金博尔·斯坦利的人。

sentences.en: My name is David Kimball Stanley, and I live on Roosevelt Island.
sentences.zh: 我叫大卫·金博尔·斯坦利，我住在罗斯福岛。

sentences.en: Well, just tell me when you want to start talking about the trash, because there isn't that much to say about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，只要告诉我你想什么时候开始聊垃圾的事就行，因为关于它其实没那么多可说的。

sentences.en: That's what's sort of funny about all this.
sentences.zh: 这就是这一切有点搞笑的地方。

sentences.en: But here, okay.
sentences.zh: 不过这里，好吧。

sentences.en: The beginning of the process is, I guess, the same as what most people deal with?
sentences.zh: 这个过程的开始，我猜，和大多数人处理的方式差不多？

sentences.en: It's just like taking out the trash.
sentences.zh: 就像倒垃圾一样。

sentences.en: You take your trash bags and then...
sentences.zh: 你拿着垃圾袋，然后……

sentences.en: We just take out a plastic bag and we tie it up.
sentences.zh: 我们只是拿出一个塑料袋，然后把它扎好。

sentences.en: And then we go outside.
sentences.zh: 然后我们走到外面。

sentences.en: Here, come with me.
sentences.zh: 来，跟我来。

sentences.en: You walk out into the hallway.
sentences.zh: 你走到走廊里。

sentences.en: We go out into the hallway.
sentences.zh: 我们走到走廊里。

sentences.en: And on each floor, there's a room, which is called the AVAX room.
sentences.zh: 在每一层楼，都有一个房间，叫做AVAX室。

sentences.en: And I've lived in Roosevelt Island my whole life.
sentences.zh: 我在罗斯福岛住了一辈子。

sentences.en: It's the same thing in at least all the original buildings, and I imagine it's the same in the newer buildings.
sentences.zh: 至少所有老建筑里都是这样，我想新建筑里也是一样。

sentences.en: But basically, every floor has a trash room.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，每层楼都有一个垃圾房。

sentences.en: Ours is right next to the stairwell.
sentences.zh: 我们的房间就在楼梯间旁边。

sentences.en: You open it up.
sentences.zh: 你把它打开。

sentences.en: And there's not a lot in it.
sentences.zh: 里面东西不多。

sentences.en: It's just this tiny little closet-like space.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个小小的、类似储藏室的空间。

sentences.en: And there's a place for recyclables.
sentences.zh: 里面有一个放可回收物的地方。

sentences.en: But stuff that isn't recyclables, you just put in this big chute.
sentences.zh: 但那些不可回收的东西，你就直接扔进这个大管道里。

sentences.en: With a little handle that you pull, and you pull open the door and throw your garbage down the chute.
sentences.zh: 带着一个小把手，你拉一下，然后拉开门，把垃圾扔进管道里。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Uh...
To be honest, it wasn't until after I left Roosevelt Island that I realized that other people don't have AVAX rooMs.
sentences.zh: 说实话，直到我离开罗斯福岛之后，我才意识到其他人是没有AVAX室的。

sentences.en: And that's not the system that's used.
sentences.zh: 而且用的也不是这种系统。

sentences.en: I'm trying to remember precisely when I learned about it.
sentences.zh: 我在努力回想自己究竟是什么时候了解到的。

sentences.en: And I think it might have been on Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 我想可能是在维基百科上看到的。

sentences.en: I, like, double-checked that I knew what pneumatic meant.
sentences.zh: 我当时还再次确认了一下自己是否知道“气动”是什么意思。

sentences.en: And was like, oh, so it just sucks the trash?
sentences.zh: 然后心想，哦，所以它只是把垃圾吸走吗？

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: And then I just, yeah, went on with my day.
sentences.zh: 然后我，嗯，就继续过我的一天了。

sentences.en: In fairness, the tubes might have made a bigger impression if Hannah and David had to put their trash bag in a rocket ship-shaped canister and fire it across the island.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，如果汉娜和大卫必须把垃圾袋装进一个火箭形状的容器里，然后把它发射到岛的另一端，这些管道可能会留下更深刻的印象。

sentences.en: But there's still something about a visit to Roosevelt Island that makes you feel like you're on the cusp of the future, even though you're clearly not.
sentences.zh: 但参观罗斯福岛总有一种奇妙的感觉，让你觉得自己正处于未来的边缘，尽管你显然并没有。

sentences.en: Hey, Molly, can I try a theory?
sentences.zh: 嘿，莫莉，我能做一个推测吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Okay, if you think about all the technology we were promised the future would hold from something like Star Trek,
sentences.zh: 好的，如果你想想《星际迷航》之类作品中我们被承诺未来会拥有的所有科技，

sentences.en: a lot of it has come true, right?
sentences.zh: 很多都变成了现实，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, we have little touchscreen computers.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们有小型触屏电脑。

sentences.en: We have hand communicators.
sentences.zh: 我们有手持通信器。

sentences.en: But one of the things that we don't have and will probably never have is the transporter,
sentences.zh: 但我们没有、而且可能永远不会有的东西之一就是传送器，

sentences.en: you know, the thing that can disassemble something somewhere and reassemble it somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那种可以在某个地方把某物拆解并在另一个地方重新组装的东西。

sentences.en: And I wonder if that has to do with why the tubes feel both so ancient and so futuristic at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这是否就是为什么这些管道让人同时感到既古老又充满未来感？

sentences.en: Like, it's the closest we ever got to transmitting a physical object instantaneously.
sentences.zh: 就像，这是我们最接近瞬间传输实体物品的一次。

sentences.en: I think that's possible.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是可能的。

sentences.en: I think that's definitely possible, that you could get something instantly, or that it's, again, that you could communicate instantly,
sentences.zh: 我觉得这绝对是可能的，你可以瞬间得到某物，或者说，同样地，你可以瞬间进行交流，

sentences.en: that you could not only get it, but you could have that feeling and that sensation or that information right away.
sentences.zh: 你不仅能得到它，还能马上拥有那种感觉、那种体验或那种信息。

sentences.en: It's the nexus of those two things.
sentences.zh: 这就是这两者的交汇点。

sentences.en: But it's more than just information.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是信息。

sentences.en: The scented handkerchief that arrives after traveling through miles of Paris Underground or even the dog biscuit from the bank teller,
sentences.zh: 那个穿过数英里巴黎地下管道送达带有香味的手帕，甚至是银行柜台送来的狗饼干，

sentences.en: these are romantic because they have physical intimacy.
sentences.zh: 这些之所以浪漫，是因为它们具有身体上的亲密感。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe that's why we keep coming back to it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许这就是为什么我们不断回想起它。

sentences.en: And maybe that's why steampunk seems important in a digital age,
sentences.zh: 也许这就是为什么蒸汽朋克在数字时代显得很重要，

sentences.en: that actually we do need physical things.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上我们确实需要实体物品。

sentences.en: And, you know, we never did get our jet packs,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们从来没有得到我们的喷气背包，

sentences.en: but we do care all the more about things that are real and tangible that come to us.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实更加关心那些送达我们手中真实而有形的事物。

sentences.en: And I think what the pneumatic post represents to us and what pneumatic tubes represent to us is the possibility that that could happen.
sentences.zh: 我认为气动传送对我们代表的意义，以及气动管道对我们代表的意义，就是这种事情可能发生的可能性。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Sam Greenspan and me, Roman Mars, with help from Muj Zady.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由萨姆·格林斯潘和我——罗曼·马尔斯共同制作，穆杰·扎迪提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It's a project of KALW 91.7 Local Public Radio in San Francisco and the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 这是旧金山KALW 91.7地方公共广播电台和旧金山美国建筑师学会的一个项目。

sentences.en: You can find this show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并点赞这个节目。

sentences.en: All of us are on Twitter, Instagram, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都在Twitter、Instagram和Spotify上。

sentences.en: But to find out more about this story, including cool pictures and links,
sentences.zh: 但要了解关于这个故事的更多信息，包括精彩的图片和链接，

sentences.en: and listen to all the episodes of 99% Invisible, you must go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 并收听《99%隐形》的所有单集，你必须访问 99pi.org。
